articles.title: Why is Harry Potter still a cheerfest for millennials?
articles.description: In this video, we explore why Harry Potter continues to cast such a powerful spell on millennials, even decades after the first book was published. From growing up alongside Harry, Ron and Hermione to eagerly waiting for every new book release, midnight launch and shocking cliffhanger, an entire generation experienced the Wizarding World in real time. But the enduring appeal of Harry Potter goes far beyond nostalgia.The video examines how Hogwarts became more than just a fictional school. For millions, it represented belonging, friendship, acceptance and the hope of finding a place where they truly fit in. It also looks at how Hogwarts Houses became early identity markers, long before social media quizzes and personality algorithms shaped online identities.As the series evolved, so did its readers. The books grew darker and more complex, tackling themes of grief, sacrifice, politics, prejudice and courage, allowing millennials to mature alongside the characters. This video breaks down why Harry Potter remains deeply personal for so many people today and how a story about magic became a defining part of an entire generation's identity, proving that some fictional worlds never really leave us.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Greek poet Archilochus: ‘The fox knows many things, but the hedgehog knows one big thing,’ what it teaches us about multitasking vs mastering one purpose
articles.description: An ancient Greek proverb, "The fox knows many things, but the hedgehog knows one big thing," offers a timeless lesson on focus. Isaiah Berlin's influential essay explored this metaphor, contrasting those with broad interests (foxes) against those with a singular, deep purpose (hedgehogs). The saying highlights the enduring power of mastering one guiding principle for significant impact, a concept still relevant in today's information-saturated world.
